EXT.evidence: Talks at length and even sings to the unborn baby despite others watching (“we’re… getting funny looks”), keeps engaging when urged to keep singing, and asks follow‑up questions about the baby’s movement.

AGR.evidence: Expresses warmth and generosity toward the baby (“you’re my baby… can’t wait to meet you… I’ll buy you a bagel and then we’ll go to the zoo”) and cooperates with others’ requests to keep singing.

CON.evidence: Says he picked his major “on a dare,” indicating a careless, impulsive decision rather than organized, deliberate planning.

NEU.evidence: Shows comfort and confidence—jokes playfully (“you’re a fetus… happy you no longer have gills”), speaks publicly without signs of anxiety, and identifies himself confidently as the baby’s dad.

OPN.evidence: Uses imaginative, playful ideas (jokes about gills/evolution), engages in creative singing, and shows curiosity by asking about the baby’s movement.
